g.text: Zoomed — how much can go before behaviour moves

text.style: font-size: 22.475px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #0b0b0b

g.text: Ablation robustness of the 4,096-component decomposition — VPD §3.2

text.style: font-size: 13.92px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #898781

g.text: VPD's version of this plot is partly a FAITHFULNESS curve: its decomposition approximates the target's weights, needs a residual Δ-component, and

text.style: font-size: 13.92px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #898781

g.text: reports CE 2.72–3.02 against a 2.71 target. Ours cannot be — the shares sum to exactly 1 per weight entry, so K=0 reproduces the model bit-for-bit

text.style: font-size: 13.92px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #898781

g.text: and there is no reconstruction error to show. This is therefore a pure MINIMALITY curve. Note the curves rise far past uniform guessing: a model with its

text.style: font-size: 13.92px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #898781

g.text: components removed is confidently wrong, not merely uninformed. Ablating a set is one elementwise mask per matrix, so all 90 points take 21 seconds.
